headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage and capability conflict: gpt-engineer writes/runs code in a shared project directory while langchain4j is an LLM framework with no isolated runtime details.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-engineer writes files in a project directory and has no self-isolation by default; langchain4j is an LLM framework with unspecified input handling. A shared project directory creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if B consumes A-authored files or prompts. The exact parser behavior is undocumented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agent_b reads agent_a-authored files or prompts from the shared project directory without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF the pair is run with a manual copy-paste bridge only, this risk drops materially.
mitigations: Separate A and B into different directories.
Require provenance tags on any file B ingests from A.
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from workspace files.
Review B's input templates for instruction delimiters.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary enforcement.

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-engineer has broad network egress and handles OPENAI_API_KEY, while langchain4j's profile does not show storage or isolation controls. If they share a workspace, A can expose generated source code or secrets through its API calls, and B may also process the same files. The shared-data path is plausible, but direct leakage evidence is absent.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share the same project directory, both can access the same generated source code.
IF agent_a sends workspace contents to a configured model backend, sensitive code may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces per agent.
Remove secrets from the shared project directory.
Restrict A's outbound network access.
Audit which files B reads before inference.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can plausibly touch the same project directory: gpt-engineer explicitly writes files and supports per-project shared state, while langchain4j has no concurrency or locking details. That creates overlapping mutable access even though B's write capability is not documented. Because B's write surface is uncertain, severity stays medium rather than high.
conditions: IF agent_b writes to the same project directory as agent_a, file clobbering or inconsistent state can occur.
IF the orchestrator provides no locking, concurrent edits can race.
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories to each agent.
Serialize writes with a lock file.
Disable concurrent runs on the same project.
Snapshot the workspace before each agent writes.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer produces code and offers to run it, while langchain4j is a framework that may consume upstream outputs as prompts or data. If B treats A's generated artifacts as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect support behavior or downstream actions. No direct verification step is documented, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a-generated code, text, or summaries without verification, errors can propagate.
IF downstream automation is attached to B, a bad A output can become an action input.
mitigations: Add a human review step before B consumes A outputs.
Require schema validation on A-produced artifacts.
Compare A outputs against source-of-truth files.
Log and diff all handoffs between agents.
requires-engineering: implement verification gates for generated content.

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-engineer explicitly handles OPENAI_API_KEY and broad network egress, while langchain4j's profile shows no data classes or residency constraints. The only concrete compliance concern is that A may transmit code or secrets to a third-party model backend; B's profile does not show a conflicting residency or retention regime. This is a limited, single-agent compliance exposure.
conditions: IF agent_a is used with regulated secrets in the project directory, those secrets may be sent to an external model provider.
IF B is configured to store prompts or logs externally, retention policy review is needed.
mitigations: Remove regulated data from the workspace.
Use a local or approved model backend for A.
Disable verbose logging.
Review retention settings before running.
requires-engineering: document and enforce data-residency controls.
